# Native delivery and terminal identity evidence

The comparison reference is unchanged Mluva v1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`. External development collectors import its public delivery and terminal-capture functions after checking both imported files byte-for-byte against that commit. Collection code stays under the worktree's ignored `tmp/`; maintained checks use Rust and the frozen observations only.

| Source file | SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| `delivery.py` | `60ce68b777eee432d5e6b06c556c8bfc5af0b7f3b3926bcf012304e66b10af46` |
| `terminal_target.py` | `c0bd12497f4fd95359834a65dfffe61706faeef1334b22163623bc287173ccb5` |

`released-delivery.json` freezes 315 independent sessions, 528 actual helper executions and callback ordering. Its SHA-256 is `a4e2cc43939cb2b7481eb999cee7e8241cd67733941c47e02c69b02279c2096e`. The helpers consume real stdin and record actual arguments; successful consuming clipboard helpers are compared with the complete synthetic UTF-8 input, including CR/LF, NUL, Unicode separators and a large pipe-sized body. The fixture covers mixed X11/Wayland environments, every released terminal basename and false title classifications, symbolic helper priority, copy-only settings, direct-edit success/failure/decline, callback errors, immediate target revalidation, one keyboard attempt, injector failure, confirmation polling and honest History receipts.

Private Unix sockets exercise live, stale, symlink, stream, regular-file, directory and absent daemon paths; owner-only permission combinations and configured/runtime/default resolution are observed without sending a datagram. The `/tmp` fallback runs only inside a new bubblewrap tmpfs and PID namespace. A helper can disappear after selection, and nonzero exit, signal termination, missing executable permission and an invalid executable remain recovery paths. Monotonic observations verify at least 110 ms between clipboard completion and keyboard dispatch against the released 120 ms settling interval. Callback and final observations independently find each helper reaped through `/proc`.

`released-terminal-target.json` freezes 123 independent sessions, 149 actions, 134 compositor queries and seven combined target/delivery cases. Its SHA-256 is `d7d50481ece67122d0f93e5d92a852be3f19ce2c4d0ca8ecfadf8c32b8e788a4`. Disposable native processes run under real allowlisted and rejected executable names; the unchanged release and Rust both resolve their identities through `/proc`. The peer supplies compositor metadata, never the capture decision, target receipt or revalidation result. A genuine `exec` changes the executable without changing the PID. Separate cases change the address/PID, unmap the target, stop its process and unlink its executable. Captured environment values remain frozen after a later environment change; each actual compositor child receives only `HYPRLAND_INSTANCE_SIGNATURE` and `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, excluding synthetic key/hook canaries.

The combined cases connect the public native target directly to the public native delivery function. The unchanged target sends one terminal chord and returns an unconfirmed receipt; changed address/PID/executable, unmapping, process exit and query timeout retain the clipboard and dispatch no keyboard helper. Neither implementation reads terminal contents, activates a window or claims a confirmed terminal insertion. Source address/type/JSON acceptance is compared, including Unicode decimal digits, underscore/trailing-space forms, arbitrary-size hexadecimal values, duplicate keys and nonfinite unused metadata. Malformed adjacent tokens remain rejected. Both stdout and stderr pipes are exercised beyond pipe capacity. Three actual elapsed half-second query failures include capture, restore and combined delivery; all query and disposable terminal processes are reaped.

The first native comparison failed the early-closed clipboard-pipe case. Its repair follows the released successful helper exit acknowledgement instead of surfacing BrokenPipe; that acknowledgement does not independently prove installed clipboard contents. Fourteen terminal controls then failed for hexadecimal parsing and nonfinite JSON acceptance, including a wrongly accepted `0x+f` address. Repairs pass the unchanged observations. These failures were recorded before the owning implementation changed; the expected results are not generated by Rust.

The owning tests are `clipboard_insertion_receipts_and_layout_safe_helpers_match_the_unchanged_release` and `terminal_capture_and_revalidation_match_actual_released_process_observations` in `delivery_contracts.rs`. Their separate risks are delivery/receipt ordering and captured compositor/process identity; combined cases verify the boundary between them. The native fixture peer is a development binary and must not be distributed. Ordinary checks require Linux `/proc` and bubblewrap for the private fallback case. They use no real clipboard, compositor, input injector, accessibility target, account credential, microphone or visible desktop.

This establishes process/receipt and controlled terminal-identity contracts. A separate [native GTK target comparison](../../../mluva-gtk/tests/fixtures/text-target-evidence.md) now verifies thirty actual accessibility cases, including a fresh client with an already-focused field, selection restoration, direct Unicode edits, password/current-focus guards and content-free delivery capture/confirmation. The present delivery suite still uses synthetic helpers. A separate [real Firefox composition](../../../mluva-gtk/tests/fixtures/firefox-target-evidence.md) now matches 21 released cases through actual clipboard/key delivery, independently observed browser edits and UTF-16 confirmation, with explicit monitored-transport controls. Broader browser/editor targets, default direct connections after corrected cold startup, ambiguous trees, Wayland/terminal insertion and full capture/controller integration remain required. Wrong-owner daemon nodes and non-UTF-8 executable paths have not been independently exercised here. Clipboard subprocess failures compare their error category and absence of later insertion; exact operating-system exception wording remains outside this component evidence. The full parity matrix stays pending, the installed app/widget remain v1.6.0 and no whole-app performance improvement is claimed.
